body:
Do you have the proprietary NVIDIA driver installed on your machine? I'm kind of surprised to see this in the verbose log for the project manager (when it uses OpenGL):

```
Found renderers:
Renderer 0: Mesa Intel(R) Graphics (RPL-P) with priority: 20
Renderer 1: zink Vulkan 1.4(NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5050 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA_PROPRIETARY)) with priority: 0
Using renderer: Mesa Intel(R) Graphics (RPL-P)
```

If you have the proprietary NVIDIA driver installed, then you always have a native OpenGL implementation available (no Zink needed). However, the open source driver (NVK) doesn't have native OpenGL support, so it needs to rely on Zink to translate OpenGL into Vulkan.

Regardless, as a workaround, I suggest opening the project directly on the [command line](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/editor/command_line_tutorial.html) with `--gpu-index 0` (or `--gpu-index 1`) to force the use of integrated graphics. For example: `godot --gpu-index 1 /path/to/project.godot`. This skips the project manager and edits the project directly with a GPU override.

To get to the bottom of the crash, you could try to [compile a custom build](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine_details/development/compiling/compiling_for_linuxbsd.html) of the `master` branch (just to make sure the issue also occurs with self-compiled builds), then try to [bisect the regression](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/feedback/bisecting.html) between those two commits:

- `good`: `4.6-stable`
- `bad`: `bf95b62586e31b8a3503f5903d7764d7c52bf2ab` (4.7-dev1)

I do have the proprietary driver (I don't exactly remember what didn't work without it, I think it was something to do with my HDMI port though).  Using `--gpu-index 0` did work around the crash.

I'll look into testing the builds and get back to you.

I did notice the final build I tested (which was this one) suddenly thought it was Godot 4.6 again (while all the other builds reported themselves as 4.7), but I assume that's unrelated.
I've noticed this is still "needs further info".  Is there something else I need to supply?

Seems to be a regression from:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/99119

But needs some more confirmation to be sure

CC @Fahien @DarioSamo

It seems like the verbose output above is from the project selector but not the actual project that hangs.  @SomethingFawful , if you can open the project that hang with verbose that would be helpful.

Something like:
```
./Godot_v4.7.1-stable_linux.x86_64 -v --path /the/path/to/the/projects/folder
```

Getting a dump from gdb would be very helpful as well.  Something like this from another terminal:
```
gdb -p 12345 -batch \
    -ex "set pagination off" \
    -ex "thread apply all bt full" \
    > godot_hang_bt.txt 2>&1
```
Just replace the 12345 with the PID for the godot process that is hung.  Should be able to find it in system monitor.  Afterward just attach the `godot_hang_bt.txt` file.

I recently upgraded from Kubuntu 24.04 to 26.04 as 24.04 was reaching End of Life, and after that upgrade the issue is no longer reproducible.  If no one else has reported this issue you can probable close this as it was only happening on a soon to be officially unsupported OS.
